supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:49 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-MLOPEZ-01 as omar.haddad with the command to execute the organization's specified Deploy-Patches.ps1 script from FILE-HD-01. It launched wusa to install a Windows update, and PowerShell exited at 13:42:39 UTC. This matches the documented patching practice and is a plausible explanation for the reported window, but does not establish the script's integrity or content.

The logs show cross-workstation account use: ben.carter obtained Kerberos tickets from WS-MLOPEZ-01 for WS-BCARTER-01 and logged on there from that workstation; shortly afterward, maria.lopez logged on to DC-HD-01 from WS-BCARTER-01. The records establish these authentications, but not whether they were authorized or malicious.

WS-MLOPEZ-01 connected to Google Drive-related and Dropbox-related endpoints. These services are not approved in the supplied inventory; the proxy records show relatively small tunnel byte counts and do not establish that files were uploaded or downloaded.
At 13:43 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01, where the recorded network logon was ANONYMOUS LOGON. The records do not identify the requested share or resource.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so activity on that host during the gap cannot be assessed from those sensors.
The proxy records for the Google Drive-related and Dropbox-related connections have user set to '-', and the supplied records do not attribute those connections to a process or person.
The available SMB records establish a connection and a logon outcome, but do not show the share or files accessed.
claims_not_established: Whether maria.lopez initiated or authorized the cross-workstation authentications.
Whether any data was transferred to Google Drive or Dropbox, or what files may have been involved.
Whether the SMB connection accessed a resource or was related to the patch deployment.
Whether the PowerShell script and patch package were authentic and unmodified.
Whether activity on WS-LPARK-01 during its collection outage is relevant to the activity under review.
additional_evidence_needed: Review WS-BCARTER-01 logon and process records, and determine whether the cross-workstation authentications were expected.
Obtain proxy or endpoint process attribution and transfer details for the Google Drive-related and Dropbox-related connections.
Review FILE-HD-01 SMB share-access and file-audit logs for the 13:43 UTC connection.
Verify the deployed patch script and package against approved versions, and review the script's execution and integrity records.
Recover or obtain alternate records for WS-LPARK-01 during the stated collection outage.
